extracted.intended_audience: communication and political-science researchers studying media, social media, and news consumption
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating experimental tests of how social endorsements and source partisan labels affect online news selection (selective exposure). Covers stimulus design, operationalization of endorsements/sources, sampling, dependent measures, and statistical modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: H1 — Partisan selection based on source cues
rubrics_metrics.description: Partisan consumers of news content will select content based on anticipated agreement (as indicated by source cues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalized by exposing participants to source labels (e.g., Fox, MSNBC) and measuring higher selection rates of ideologically congruent sources among partisans; compare mean selection rates by party identification and test with directional (one-tailed) t-tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: H2 — Use of social endorsements as a selection heuristic
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers of news content will use social endorsements to make content selections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present aggregated social recommendation cues (e.g., 'N people recommend', 'Most Emailed' ranks) and measure increased probability of selecting strongly endorsed items versus weakly endorsed items; analyze via selection rates vs chance and infer bandwagon/bandwagon-like heuristic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: H3 — Social endorsements outweigh perceived partisan alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: News consumers will be more likely to utilize social endorsements than perceived partisan alignment of a news source (selective exposure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare conditions with partisan labels only, endorsements only, and both; expect endorsement-driven selections to reduce partisan selection differences to chance levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: H4 — Presence of social endorsements negates source-cue effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence of social endorsements will negate the effect of source cues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test interaction effects: when endorsements are present, partisan alignment coefficients on source should lose significance in choice models; check robustness across experimental conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heuristic processing / bounded rationality as rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: People rely on heuristics (e.g., source, social endorsements, story title) because full optimization of many-item news choice is cognitively infeasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifies using simple, salient cues in experiments and expecting satisficing rather than exhaustive utility calculations; design manipulations (e.g., time pressure) to encourage heuristic processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social endorsements convey utility/popularity/social relevance (bandwagon heuristic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregated recommendations/popularity cues suggest that others find the content relevant/valuable and thus serve as a decision-relevant heuristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bandwagon heuristic components: (a) assume others' support predicts personal relevance, (b) use others' attitudes to form opinions, (c) follow the crowd when many endorse an item; experimental manipulations should vary endorsement strength to capture these effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source cues convey reputation, trust, and perceived ideology
rubrics_metrics.description: Source labels primarily convey the reputation and ideology/partisan slant of the news organization and serve as a heuristic for anticipated agreement or credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and label sources with known ideological valence (e.g., Fox = right, MSNBC = left, USA Today/Reuters = neutral) and conduct manipulation checks to confirm perceived ideology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus design — headline + optional source logo and/or endorsement cue
rubrics_metrics.description: Each news item presentation should include at minimum the headline; depending on condition, display a source logo and/or a social endorsement cue (Facebook-like icon + 'N number of people recommend').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use real headlines pulled in real time (RSS) for ecological validity; create experimental cells that separately manipulate partisan labels and social endorsements (partisan-only, endorsement-only, both).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalization of endorsement strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Endorsements should be operationalized at distinct levels: 'low' endorsements (randomly generated small numbers) and 'high' endorsements (very large numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study 1 example ranges: low = 0–1,000 recommendations; high = >10,000 recommendations (ranges informed by monitoring real-world 'recommends'); Study 2 example: Facebook-like ranges 1–35 or 150–650 and 'most emailed' ranks 1–5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source labeling and partisan assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign source labels with known or assumed partisan alignments (Fox for right, MSNBC for left, neutral labels like USA Today and Reuters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base assignments on prior literature and empirical perceptions; perform manipulation checks that ask participants to rate source ideology to confirm labels function as intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice task dependent measure — selecting one of multiple unordered alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the participant's choice of one article from a set (e.g., four items) as the dependent variable; choices are unordered categorical alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the choice is among unordered alternatives, model with multinomial/conditional logit frameworks rather than binary or ordered logits; aggregate across trials at the individual level to compute mean selection rates to avoid inflating observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental stimuli composition — topic categories (hard vs soft)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include multiple topic categories (e.g., two 'hard' categories: World News, Business; two 'soft' categories: Sports, Entertainment) to test generality across content types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Randomize story assignment across endorsement and source conditions within topic sets to control for topical effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and subject recruitment considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use online crowd-sourcing (Mechanical Turk) to recruit a national sample of active internet users but recognize limitations in representativeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include validation questions to ensure compliance; report demographic distributions, note over/underrepresentation relative to census, and caution about generalizability beyond active internet users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate vs chance comparison for endorsement impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare observed selection rates for high-endorsement items to expected chance rates (e.g., 25% when one of four items is high-endorsed) to measure the effect of endorsements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute percent greater/less than chance as (observed_rate − chance_rate) / chance_rate and test differences with chi-square tests; present visualization and statistical contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical modeling — mixed multinomial (conditional logit) specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Model unordered choice using a conditional logit or mixed multinomial logit with alternative-specific and individual-level predictors, allowing for random effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate by simulating random parameters and maximizing likelihood (e.g., Newton–Raphson); implement using software like the 'mlogit' R package; include interaction terms (e.g., respondent ideology × source) to test partisan selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of directional hypothesis testing and effect-size reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Because hypotheses are directional, use one-tailed tests (e.g., one-tailed t-tests) where appropriate and report effect sizes such as Cohen's d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about directional testing choices; accompany p-values with effect sizes to convey practical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of chi-square tests and effect-size phi for proportion comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: For categorical comparisons (e.g., selections vs chance), use chi-square tests and report φ as an effect-size measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when comparing observed vs expected counts or proportions across conditions (e.g., high-endorsement selection > chance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Model fit and information criteria — prefer AIC/BIC over pseudo R2
rubrics_metrics.description: For mixed logit models, pseudo R2 measures offer little utility; instead report model fit using AIC and BIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain limitations of pseudo R2 for mixed models and provide likelihood-based fit statistics (log-likelihood, LRT χ2) alongside AIC/BIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecological validity in stimulus and interface design
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximize ecological validity by using authentic, real-time news stories, visually realistic cues, and feed-back mechanisms that mirror true news aggregators and social media platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borrow real-world social endorsement formats (e.g., Facebook 'N people like this', most-emailed lists) and integrate realistic timers and browsing interfaces to simulate naturalistic user experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time pressure as a manipulation to encourage heuristic processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Including a timer can induce time pressure, which reduces information search and increases heuristic processing, potentially strengthening manipulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that time pressure may amplify endorsement and source cue effects; report this design choice and consider its influence when generalizing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulation checks for perceived source ideology
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct manipulation checks where participants rate each news source on an ideology scale to confirm that sources are perceived as intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report means and standard deviations for perceived ideology and test that each source mean differs from the midpoint in the expected direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of individual-level recommender attributes as limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that individual-level recommendations (e.g., from friends) may be moderated by attributes like similarity/homophily, attraction, perceived status, and thus could alter endorsement effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge limitation if study uses aggregate endorsements only; suggest future work to manipulate recommender identity and attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data aggregation to avoid inflated observation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate each individual's selections across multiple trials (e.g., compute mean selection rate per source across four topics) to avoid treating repeated choices as independent observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use per-individual summary measures when reporting simple comparisons; use appropriate multilevel or choice models to account for repeated measures in inferential analyses.
